Definition 4.1 requires the triangle inequality. Definition 4.2 (PDF p. 19/printed p. 957) then defines \[M\leq^*N\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \dim M_p\leq\dim N_p\quad\mbox{for every }p,\] and \[d_E(M,N)=\inf\{\varepsilon\geq0:
       \operatorname{Er}_\varepsilon(M)\leq^*N,\ 
       \operatorname{Er}_\varepsilon(N)\leq^*M\}.\] This formula fails the stated requirement, already for pfd one-parameter modules.

Definition 4.1 requires the triangle inequality. Definition 4.2 (PDF p. 19/printed p. 957) then defines \[M\leq^*N\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad

edits.before: Take the two-parameter modules \[M=0,\qquad N=k_{[0,1)^2},\qquad \varepsilon=1,\] with diagonal shifts. Zero maps give an \(\varepsilon\)-interleaving because both \(2\varepsilon\) structure maps vanish. However, \(\operatorname{Pru}_\varepsilon(M)=0\), while \[\operatorname{EN}_0(N)=\{N\}\quad\mbox{up to isomorphism}.\] Consequently \(0\) is not a \(2r\varepsilon=0\) refinement of the nonzero module \(N\), contrary to Theorem 5.4(ii). The same example gives \[d_I(0,N)=f_R(0,N)=\frac12>0,\] whereas the right side of Corollary 5.6 is zero.
